Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http: Ilwvwv.dilg.com.ph DILG OPINION No. 32 s. 2023 MAY 04 2023 HON. ORLY A. AMIT Sangguniang Panlalawigan Member 2nd Legislative District Province of Davao del Norte Dear Hon. Amit: This has reference to your letter dated November 18, 2022 seeking legal opinion from this Department regarding the following: l. What are the technical differences between the terms "Peace and Order" and "Public Safety" as provided in the DILG Memorandum Circular (MC) No. 2022- 118 dated 19 September 2022; 2. Whether concreting of road and/or maintenance projects and the likes can be considered as project under Peace and Order Program (POP) or Public Safety Program; and 3. Whether the computation of the thirty percent (30%) Confidential Fund is based solely on the total Peace and Order Program Fund or the total amount of the combined Peace and Order and Public Safety Fund. Per your letter, the Sangguniang Panlalawigan of Davao del Norte, through the Committee on Finance, Budget and Appropriations is currently reviewing the proposed Calendar Year (CY) 2023 General Fund Annual Budget of the Province, which includes Programs, Projects and Activities (PPA) categorized as Peace and Order Program. You also represented that you are requesting for the opinion in aid of legislation. Hence, the queries. We will answer the first and second queries in one discussion since they are interrelated. We invite your attention to Section 4 of the DILG Memorandum Circular No. 2019- 143 or the Omnibus Guidelines for Peace and Order Councils (POCs) dated August 27 , 2019 where the terms "Peace and Order Program" (POP), "Peace and Order and Public Safety (POPS) Plan", and "Public Safety Programs" were defined, to wit: "4.10. Peace and Order Programs (POP) includes projects, programs, and "Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

activities (PPAs) that directly address criminality, armed conflict, and human right violations and bring about the achievement of justice, peace and order. It can also be any or combination of PPAs enumerated in Section 3.23 of JMC No. 2015-01, dated January 9, 2015. Xxxx 4.13 Public Safety Programs (PSP) covers activities that protect the community from danqers threateninq their qeneral welfare and safety, and address the focus areas of: (i) road and vehicle safety, (ii) jail management and (iii) emergency/crisis management and fire safety." (Emphasis ours) While DILG MC No. 2022-118 dated 19 September 2022 defines the Peace and Order and Public Safety Plan (POPS Plan), to wit: "The POPS plan is a three-year comprehensive and concerted action plan, consisting of programs and activities, that aims to promote and attain a safe, secure, peaceful and progressive community. Xxxx it shall be formulated and approved within 200 days (not later than January 15), after a newly elected LCE assumes office.' From the foregoing, Peace and Order Programs includes projects, programs, and activities (PPAs) that directly address criminality, armed conflict, and human right violations and bring about the achievement of justice, peace and order. On the other hand, Public Safety Programs includes activities that protect the community from dangers threatening their general welfare and safety, which also address the area of road and vehicle safety. Thus, the concreting of road and/or maintenance projects and the likes can be considered as projects under Public Safety Programs (PSP). With regard to the last query, we likewise invite your attention to Sections 4.1.3 and 5.1.3.1 of COA-DBM-DILG-GCG-DND Joint Circular No. 2015-01 dated January 8, 2015 regarding the computation of the 30%, to wit: "4.1.3 LGUs whose peace and order is a priority concern and which have duly allocated CF, but not IF, in their annual appropriation ordinances, provided, that specific amount for POP is included in their Peace and Order and Public Safety Plan and, provided further, that there is a specific appropriation for POP in their annual budget. The computation of allowable CF of an LGU shall be based on the budget of the LGU's POP only. 5.1.3.1 LGUs with peace and order concerns shall allocate in their respective Annual Appropriations Ordinance funds for POP, as part of its Peace and Order and Public Safety Plan, as required under 4.1.3 of this Joint Circular. The total amount of CF shall not exceed thirty percent (30%) of the total amount allocated for the LGU's POP." (Emphasis and underlining supplied) Page 2 of 3

The above-cited provisions are clear that the computation of the thirty percent (30%) Confidential Fund shall be based on the budget of the LGU's Peace and Order Programs (POP) only. A cardinal rule in statutory construction is that when the law is clear and free from any doubt or ambiguity, there is no room for construction or interpretation. There is only room for application. As the statute is clear, plain, and free from ambiguity, it must be given its literal meaning and applied without attempted interpretation. 1 The opinion of this Department is based solely on the facts and representations you have narrated in your letter and our appreciation of the same. We hope to have addressed your concern accordingly. Thank you. Very truly yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: AN VICTOR R.
